result.answer: Yes, a resend now could have done harm. The failed message moved the patient to WARD-B, bed BAY2-04, at 08:20 UTC. The bed-management system never applied it and has no receipt for it. It then applied a later transfer to WARD-C, bed BAY1-07, at 08:45 UTC (version 2). Resending the 08:20 UTC transfer would put the patient back on a ward they had already left. Sending nothing keeps the record matching the PAS's latest word. The cost is that the short stop on WARD-B is missing from the movement history. The members agree on this. Their views differ only in focus. Encounter says the message's intent no longer holds. Impact warns that systems reading the record, such as the bed board, could then show the wrong bed. It also says Shutter cannot see those systems. Conformance says the message itself is well formed. The failure was the receiver being unavailable (HTTP 503), so the content was never judged. Being valid does not make a resend safe. Under the alternative in W1, a site that keeps a full movement history, this case would have gone to a person instead of closing with no write. That does not apply here. The board can only answer questions. It cannot resend or approve anything.

perspectives.view: The 08:20 UTC transfer to WARD-B was overtaken by the applied 08:45 UTC transfer to WARD-C. A resend would contradict the PAS's latest word, so the right outcome is to send nothing.

A resend would most likely do harm. It would put the patient back on WARD-B in the record, and systems that read the record could then show the wrong bed. Shutter cannot see those systems. Not acting only leaves the WARD-B stop out of the history.

The ADT^A02 message is well formed and matches the route's version. The failure was the receiver being unavailable, not the content. But being valid is not the same as being safe to resend, and on that it agrees with sending nothing.

setting.why: The bed-management system is set to keep only the patient's current place, not a full movement history, so the overtaken transfer closed with nothing sent.

under_alternative.why: With a full movement history, the case would have gone to a person instead of closing as superseded.

response.content: I submitted the board's answer: yes, resending would have put the patient back on WARD-B, a ward they had already left, so sending nothing was right.
